title: South Korea’s Kospi stock index is falling: Why AI chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung are facing investor jitters
excerpt: With concerns about over-investment growing, the Korea Composite Stock Price Index is down a dramatic 32% over the last month.
content_html:
Sarah Fielding

Wed, July 29, 2026 at 8:06 AM EDT 1 min read

It's no secret that investors are getting nervous about AI, leaving chipmakers' shares struggling.

Most Read from Fast Company

  • Internet-famous bald eagle Jackie is fighting for her life as donations pour in to save Big Bear habitat

  • How to make Google Maps and Apple Maps show you the actual fastest route, every time

  • Medicare Part D subsidy program: Why Trump is ending it and what it could mean for prescription drug costs

Wednesday brought further evidence with South Korea's Kospi (Korea Composite Stock Price Index) falling another 6%. The stock index is down over 32% in just the last month. 

The significant decline follows poor performance from two of the Kospi Index's biggest stocks: SK Hynix Inc. (KSE: 000660.KS) and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. (KSE: 005930.KS).

The two chip manufacturers have struggled recently as over-investment becomes a growing fear in the AI world. 

SK Hynix closed over 9.6% down after falling more than 19% during the day. Its shares are down more than 45% in the last month.

Samsung had fallen more than 5.2% at close and is down over 35% in a month. 

Shares of SK Hynix also took a hit after the company failed to meet analysts' expectations. On Wednesday, the company announced its second-quarter results, including 79.32 trillion won ($54.64 billion) in revenue. 

While it was a 51% jump from last quarter, it fell short of predictions for $84 trillion won ($57.86 billion), according to consensus estimates cited by CNBC.

Operating profit also came in lower than expected, with a reported 60.54 trillion won ($41.70 billion) compared to 64 trillion won ($44.10 billion). 

Outside of South Korea, chip manufacturers such as Nvidia Corporation and Micron Technology have also had tough weeks.

Over the last five days, Nvidia's shares (Nasdaq: NVDA) fell 7.1% and Micron's dropped 14.48%.

2026 年 7 月 29 日星期三，美国东部时间上午 8:06 阅读 1 分钟

众所周知，投资者对人工智能感到紧张，导致芯片制造商的股价陷入困境。

大多数阅读来自《快公司》

  • 网络名人秃鹰杰基正在为自己的生命而战，捐款纷至沓来，以拯救大熊的栖息地
  • 如何让 Google 地图和 Apple 地图每次都向您显示实际最快的路线
  • 医疗保险 D 部分补贴计划：特朗普为何终止该计划以及该计划对处方药成本意味着什么

周三，韩国 Kospi（韩国综合股价指数）又下跌 6%，进一步证明了这一点。 仅上个月该股指就下跌了32%以上。

此次大幅下跌是由于 Kospi 指数最大的两只股票 SK 海力士公司 (KSE: 000660.KS) 和三星电子有限公司 (KSE: 005930.KS) 表现不佳所致。

随着过度投资成为人工智能领域日益令人担忧的问题，这两家芯片制造商最近陷入困境。

SK 海力士当天跌幅超过 19%，收盘跌幅超过 9.6%。 上个月其股价下跌超过 45%。

三星收盘跌幅超过 5.2%，一个月内跌幅超过 35%。

SK海力士的股价也因未能达到分析师的预期而受到打击。 周三，该公司公布了第二季度业绩，其中收入为 79.32 万亿韩元（546.4 亿美元）。

根据 CNBC 援引的共识估计，虽然较上季度增长 51%，但仍低于 84 万亿韩元（578.6 亿美元）的预测。

营业利润也低于预期，为 60.54 万亿韩元（417 亿美元），而 64 万亿韩元（441 亿美元）。

在韩国之外，英伟达公司和美光科技等芯片制造商也经历了艰难的几周。

过去五天里，英伟达 (NASDAQ: NVDA) 股价下跌 7.1%，美光 (Micron) 股价下跌 14.48%。
